name: Community Assessment of Psychic Experiences
developer: Stefanis, Hanssen, Smirnis, Avramopoulos, Evdokimidis, Stefanis, Verdoux and van Os (2002)
construct: Lifetime frequency of, and distress from, psychotic like experiences in the community across positive, negative and depressive dimensions.
licence: CamCOPS: Intellectual property "Public domain/freeware"; "totally freeware" (personal communication, Jim van Os to Rudolf Cardinal, 2014-10-16).
instructions: Not reproduced in the CamCOPS string file beyond the distress stem "Please indicate how distressed you are by this experience:". The printed CAPE-42 asks respondents to rate how often they have had each experience, then, if the experience occurs at least sometimes, how distressed they are by it.

subscales.name: Positive
subscales.description: Delusional ideation, paranoia, grandiosity, thought interference and hallucinations. Membership confirmed from the Cambridge supplementary table.

subscales.name: Negative
subscales.description: Avolition, social withdrawal, affective flattening and anergia.

subscales.name: Depressive
subscales.description: Sadness, pessimism, guilt, tension and suicidal ideation.

scoring: Each item is rated for frequency 1 (Never) to 4 (Nearly always); items rated Sometimes or higher are also rated for distress 1 (Not distressed) to 4 (Very distressed), with Never frequency recorded as Not distressed (1). For each dimension compute a frequency sum and a distress sum, usually reported as weighted means (sum divided by the number of items answered) so that scores range 1 to 4. A weighted severity score can also be computed by multiplying each item's frequency by its distress. Higher scores indicate more frequent or more distressing experiences. No diagnostic cut off; the CAPE-P15 positive short form uses a weighted mean of 1.47 as a risk threshold in some studies, and a weighted severity positive score above 1.75 has been proposed as a detector of at risk status.
citation: Stefanis, N. C., Hanssen, M., Smirnis, N. K., Avramopoulos, D. A., Evdokimidis, I. K., Stefanis, C. N., Verdoux, H., & van Os, J. (2002). Evidence that three dimensions of psychosis have a distribution in the general population. Psychological Medicine, 32(2), 347–358. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0033291701005141
transcriptionNote: The itemsUrl cape42.homestead.com now returns "Sorry, the site you requested has been disabled". The 42 frequency items were transcribed from the CamCOPS cape42.xml string file (q1 to q42), which matches the item order on psytests.org. Each frequency item has a matching distress item with the stem "Please indicate how distressed you are by this experience:" and options Not distressed, A bit distressed, Quite distressed, Very distressed (1 to 4); these 42 distress items are recorded in each item note rather than as separate item objects. Respondent instructions for the frequency scale were not reproduced in any fetched source. The 20 Positive items were matched by wording to the Cambridge supplementary table (S0924933800015510sup004.pdf), which lists them without numbers. No open source reachable with WebFetch gave the item numbers for the Negative and Depressive dimensions (PMC pages were blocked by a browser check), so the remaining 22 items are coded "Negative or Depressive (dimension not confirmed from source)" and should be assigned from the original scoring key before use. Second pass: Negative and Depressive memberships resolved from the CamCOPS cape42.py task source (https://camcops.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_modules/camcops_server/tasks/cape42.html).
